By Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala
 Ernakulam.
By Public Prosecutor Sri. Rajesh Vijayan

THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION  ON 02-03-2012, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
DSV/-
 P.S.GOPINATHAN, J.
O R D E R

In this petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the petitioners, who are accused Nos.1 to 5 in Crime No.33/2011 of Kuttampuzha Excise Range for offence under Section 57(a) of the Abkari Act, assails Annexure A Crime and Occurrence Report registered by the Excise Inspector, Kuttampuzha.

2. Having heard either side, I find that the petitioners are the employees and licensee of toddy shop No.03 of Koovapara and on 30/08/2011, the Food Inspector, Perumbavoor took a sample of toddy from the toddy shop run by the petitioners.
After analysis, as per Annexure C report, it was reported that the sample contained artificial sweetener saccharine.
Ethanol content was reported below the level prescribed by the Food Safety and Standards Rules and Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Rules and Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Consequently,
Annexure A Crime and occurrence reported was registered.

3. The plea of the petitioners is that only one sample was taken and that Rule 8 of the Kerala Abkari Shops Disposal Rules 2002 mandates that two samples should be taken so that in the event the aggrieved person assails the first report, he could get an opportunity to send the second sample for analysis through court and get a second opinion.
By taking only one sample, that opportunity was denied.

The learned counsel in support of the argument relied upon the decision of this court in Gireesh Kumar V. State of Kerala (2010 (2) KLJ 444) wherein, in an identical case, this court quashed all further proceedings in pursuance to the case registered against the petitioner therein.

entities.text: Gireesh Kumar V. State of Kerala (2010 (2) KLJ 444)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
C.Y.Sajeev vs State Of Kerala on 2 March, 2012 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31101850/
2 4.

The learned Government Pleader fairly conceded that only one sample was taken by the Food Inspector and it is not in accordance with Rule 8 and the case on hand is identical to Gireesh Kumar's case (Supra).
However, the learned Government Pleader would submit that whether the failure to take second sample would cause prejudice to the petitioners is a matter of evidence.
Irrespective of the above argument, the learned Government Pleader could not point out any thing to have a different decision than the one in Gireesh Kumar's case (Supra).
In the above circumstance, following the above decision, I find that it would be appropriate to quash all further proceedings in pursuance to Annexure A.
In the result, this petition is allowed and all further proceedings in pursuance to Annexure A would stand quashed.

P.S.GOPINATHAN JUDGE DSV/-
